exposure: caesarean section indications (multiple previous C-section, fetal distress, breech position of fetus, cephalo-pelvic disproportion (CPD), pregnancy induced hypertension (PIH), gestational diabetes (GDM), Twins/triplets, Cord prolapsed, oligohydramnios, Polyhydramnios, placenta previa)
outcome: common complications of spinal anesthesia (low back pain, difficulty in urination)
cohort: The study included 400 women who had undergone C-section surgeries under either general or epidural anesthesia in district Rawalpindi.
finding: The study found that spinal anesthesia was more frequent than general anesthesia for C-sections, primarily due to previous caesareans and fetal distress, with low back pain and difficulty in urination being reported as common complications after spinal anesthesia.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from July 2016 to January 2017.
